properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA family implementations declared in the lockfile: js-sha3@0.8.0 (Keccak/SHA-3), hash.js@1.1.7 (SHA-1/SHA-2 via elliptic), crypto-js@4.2.0 (SHA-1/SHA-2), and @noble/hashes (SHA-2/SHA-3, the keystore's live provider). SHA-2/SHA-3 at 256 bits are PQ-acceptable; the SHA-1 entries are the weak spots. Dependency inventory; live SHA use in the repo's own code is Keccak-256 (ALG-052c24b2), SHA-256 (noble, keystore HMAC) and the two SHA-1 sites under ALG-725ecd3e.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: MD5 in the lockfile via apache-md5@1.1.8, a dependency of verdaccio-htpasswd@13.1.5 — verdaccio (the local npm registry devDependency used in e2e publish tests) uses it for Apache-style htpasswd password entries. MD5-crypt is a deprecated, weak password hash (CWE-328; quantum-relevant only via Grover). Dev-tooling dependency only; no MD5 call site exists in the repo's own code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: bcrypt-pbkdf@1.0.2 is declared in the pnpm lockfile as a transitive dependency (OpenSSH private-key format KDF, pulled in via the sshpk/http-signature chain used by legacy tooling). The lockfile declaration is the asset; no bcrypt KDF call site exists in this repo's own code. bcrypt itself is a password KDF, quantum-relevant only via Grover's quadratic speedup.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA available in the shipped dependency tree: elliptic@6.6.1 (depended on via the jwa→ecdsa-sig-formatter chain of the JWT tooling) implements ECDSA over secp256k1, P-256/384/521, Ed25519 and ECDH. ECDSA is quantum-vulnerable (Shor). The repo's own live ECDSA use is Ethereum secp256k1 via EDR/ethers (see secp256k1 object ALG-673c8f24); elliptic itself is not imported by workspace source.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 capability in the shipped dependency tree via tweetnacl@0.14.5 (and @noble/curves through ethers). Ed25519 signatures are quantum-vulnerable (Shor breaks Edwards-curve DLP); migration target ML-DSA or SLH-DSA. No live Ed25519 call site in the workspace's own source; dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 — the SHA-3-family hash Ethereum standardizes — used pervasively across this Ethereum toolchain: chai-matchers compute event/data hashes for assertions, hardhat-ethers register EDR's native keccak256 into ethers, and hardhat-utils wraps ethereum-cryptography's keccak256 for build/cache identity. 125 sites in 29 files, all the same hashing pattern over public blockchain/config data. Keccak-256 is PQ-acceptable (128-bit post-Grover). Confirmed at object level after sampling production a

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-GCM available in the shipped @noble/ciphers library (declared via packages/hardhat-keystore/package.json). The keystore application itself instantiates the misuse-resistant SIV variant: gcmsiv(encryptionKey, iv) at encryption.ts:252/277 (AES-256-GCM-SIV with a random 12-byte IV and 256-bit key). AES-GCM(-SIV) is symmetric AEAD — PQ-relevant only via Grover's halving to 128-bit security, which remains acceptable.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ChaCha20-Poly1305 available in the shipped @noble/ciphers library (declared via packages/hardhat-keystore/package.json). No call site in the application code — the keystore uses AES-256-GCM-SIV instead. Presence in the shipped library is the inventory fact; strong PQ-acceptable AEAD either way.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: XSalsa20-Poly1305 in the lockfile — the secretbox AEAD of the tweetnacl library declared transitively in pnpm-lock.yaml. No call site in this repo's own code; presence in the shipped dependency tree is the inventory fact. Salsa20 is a pre-quantum-era stream cipher but the Poly1305 MAC and 256-bit key leave it PQ-acceptable in practice; superseded by ChaCha20-Poly1305 and AES-GCM-SIV.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 declared transitively in the lockfile. Ships Ed25519 signatures, X25519 ECDH and XSalsa20-Poly1305 — all quantum-vulnerable except the symmetric part — a 2016-era crypto library, superseded upstream by noble libraries. Not imported by the workspace's own source; presence in the shipped dependency tree is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider for the hardhat keystore: @noble/hashes 2.x (declared in packages/hardhat-keystore/package.json) supplies scrypt, HMAC-SHA256, SHA-256 and other hashes; the keystore calls its scrypt, hmac, sha256 and randomBytes (which draws on the runtime CSPRNG). properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider for the hardhat keystore: @noble/ciphers 2.4.0 (declared in packages/hardhat-keystore/package.json) supplies the AEAD used to encrypt keystore secrets — the keystore calls gcmsiv (AES-256-GCM-SIV) from @noble/ciphers/aes.js. The library also ships AES-GCM/CBC/CTR, ChaCha20-Poly1305 and XSalsa20-Poly1305 implementations.
